props.title: a2 FMM Burndown
props.subtitle: 15 rows, four stories — one design ruling unblocks eleven of them

props.content: This week's projection regeneration enrolled the April bulk-PE corpus into the a2 scorecard (85 → 218 rows). Transcripts for every enrolled row are verified fresh — these failures are real, and they cluster cleanly.

props.label: TRANSCRIPT AUDIT
props.title: Did we regen ASR for these rows? Yes — verified three ways

props.content:
Every enrolled a2 row has an entry in `data/src/partner_graph/output/fixtures/transcriptions.jsonl`. Per row: **①** ledger `clean_text` matches the current source utterance, **②** the runtime consumed exactly the whisper transcript (candidate text `OPEN FLIGHT PLAN` == whisper `open flight plan.`), **③** whisper↔gold divergence is normal ASR orthography (*One Seven → 17*), not staleness.

No fix on this page requires re-transcription. The only authoring change (cluster C) adds output-side `expected_radio_speech_text`, which never touches fixture audio.

props.title: Freshness verdict
props.content: Projection AND transcription are current for all 218 enrolled a2 rows. These are honest pipeline failures, not fixture debt.

props.label: CLUSTER A · 11 ROWS · BLOCKED
props.title: Pilot-request FMM over-acceptance
props.subtitle: Gold says no_match; runtime accepts. Discriminator proven: every passing no_match sibling has an EMPTY parse — a successfully parsed pilot request always becomes an accepted proposal.

props.title: Deliberately blocked — both cheap fixes are traps
props.content: Rewriting gold to match runtime stamps behavior into truth (authority inversion). Gating proposals in Python hardcodes policy. The conflict is real: command_parameter_contract.yaml:174 defines comm_request with an executable request_event — accept may be the intended contract — while gold and all 23 passing (empty-parse) siblings encode no_match.

props.label: THE RULING
props.title: Two resolutions — pick one, all 11 rows unblock
Path 1 — no_match is canonical
props.content:
Pilot-initiated requests never carry command authority; the runtime over-accepts.

Fix: gate proposal-building on speaker/addressing scope in DISPATCH POLICY (typed YAML via modules/authority — never a Python tuple). Gold untouched.

Risk: policy gate must not suppress legitimate ownship-directed commands.

props.title: Path 2 — accept-with-request_event is canonical
props.content:
The contract already defines comm_request with executable request_event; FMM should track what the pilot asked for.

Fix: update gold on the 11 rows via partner SOURCE + regeneration, and audit the 23 empty-parse siblings whose no_match has never actually been exercised.

Risk: bare check-ins (A3) accepted as requests suggests acceptance is too broad even under this path.

props.title: Fix contract
props.content: ① slot-equivalence policy (never scorer-side) · ② pick the canonical key in the command contract, align gold · ③ align gold slot shape with contract · ④ one extractor fix in modules/intent/emergency.py — which is also a cognitive-43 complexity hotspot, so the bugfix and decomposition can share a slice. Q10 'full redesign' stays a separate structural decision.

props.content: The remaining a2 fails break at intent_classification (23) / parameter_extraction (13 incl. the 6 emergency rows kept here). Triage with the full row list is appended to `plan-bugfix-a1-a2-operational-row-burndown.md`: 24 `pe_bulk_*` singles, `ctaf_broadcast` clusters in `pe_taxi_out_non_towered` (3) and `pe_v3_proof_pack` (5), plus assorted proof-pack and module rows.

props.title: Investigation hint for that lane
props.content: Many rows show exp=X obs=X yet fail intent_classification — the label matches but candidate/segment structure fails. Check first-candidate scope before assuming label misses.
